ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Harriet Tubman — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mrs. Tubman returns for her subsequent annual wellness visit, two weeks after a sick visit for viral gastroenteritis. She completed the health risk assessment before the visit. The illness resolved within four days; she restarted candesartan once she was eating and drinking normally, and the light-headedness has gone. Since her last wellness visit she has had no falls, emergency visits, or hospital stays. She takes candesartan and modafinil every day, uses acetaminophen about once a week, and has taken no ibuprofen since the spring. Her headache diary shows headache days holding near the August level. With modafinil and two scheduled naps, unplanned sleep episodes are again rare and happen only while she is seated. She does not drive. She runs a busy household and is active in her church. Her one concern is safety at home if a sleep episode comes on while she is cooking or bathing. [S]

Subsequent annual wellness visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed, personalized prevention plan updated, and a written copy given. Depression, alcohol, and cognitive screens are negative. [S]
Next annual wellness visit in one year.

Viral gastroenteritis with a prerenal creatinine rise, resolved (A08.4). Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL (eGFR 67) on candesartan, back to her baseline. [S]
No further testing for this illness.
Sick-day rule: hold candesartan on any day she has vomiting or diarrhea and cannot keep fluids down, and restart when she can.

Chronic post-traumatic headache (G44.329). Improved on candesartan, without medication overuse. Blood pressure 126/76 mmHg. [S]
Continue candesartan 16 mg daily and the headache diary.
Acetaminophen no more than 2 days a week; no NSAIDs.

Provisional narcolepsy without cataplexy (G47.429). Improved on modafinil and scheduled naps; episodes are rare and only while seated. [S]
Continue modafinil 100 mg each morning and two scheduled naps.
Home safety for sleep episodes: cook with a timer and stay in the kitchen while the stove is on, or use the microwave when tired; take showers instead of tub baths, or bathe only when someone else is home; no ladders or step stools; keep things she uses often within reach.
She does not drive; she should not start driving without first discussing it with her sleep specialist.

Fall risk. Low by screening, with no falls in the past year and a Timed Up and Go of 10 seconds. Sudden sleep episodes and the light-headedness she had during dehydration are her main risks. [S]
Add a second stair handrail.
Continue daily walking and housework for strength and balance.
Sit down at once if she feels a sleep episode coming on.

Follow-up: DXA scan, lipid panel, and hepatitis C test ordered; FIT kit to return by mail. COVID-19 vaccine at her pharmacy. Headache and sleep review with her neurologist on its usual schedule. Next annual wellness visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent and at her pace. She has named a health care agent and completed a written health care directive today; a copy is now in the chart. Her faith guides her decisions. She wants full treatment for reversible illness, including hospital care. She would not want resuscitation or prolonged life support if she could no longer know the people around her. She will share these wishes with her agent. [S]
